lab_indicators_24h.note: National aggregate: Ituri 113 samples documented in the collection network / 42 positive (29 living, 13 deaths) = 37.2%; Nord-Kivu 126 received and analyzed / 8 positive (5 living, 3 deaths) = 6.3%. Positivity uses 50 positives over 239 analyzed samples (Ituri + Nord-Kivu); Haut-Uele, Tshopo and Sud-Kivu report no laboratory block this cycle and are excluded from the denominator rather than counted as zero. The day's laboratory positives (42 + 8 = 50) EQUAL the day's confirmations exactly, as at SitRep65 and SitRep66. Ituri's documented denominator fell 167 -> 113 while positivity fell 41.9% -> 37.2%; a shrinking denominator alongside a shrinking case count is a testing-volume movement and must not be read as measured prevalence. A diagnostic laboratory was installed in Logo (Ituri).

care_continuity: SitRep67 Tableau 6: 737 in isolation at end of day (286 confirmed / 451 suspected, a split that closes exactly against the census) at 86.7% global bed occupancy (737/850 beds); Ituri 78.4% (556/709), Nord-Kivu 128.4% (181/141) and still saturated; Haut-Uele and Tshopo report ND. The bed identity closes exactly at every level (700 J-1 + 180 admissions - 143 exits = 737; Ituri 536 + 118 - 98 = 556; Nord-Kivu 164 + 62 - 45 = 181). Exits over 24h (143 total): 27 deaths, 96 non-cases, 13 recoveries, 7 escapes, 0 HGR transfers. Ituri first-line personnel: 121 cumulative infections, 67 recovered, 18 hospitalized, 36 deaths (CFR 29.8%), unchanged from SitRep66 and internally consistent across all ten zone rows.

Ituri bed capacity did NOT contract this cycle. Ituri bed capacity across SitRep62-67 reads 693, 693, 700, 706, 798, 709, and occupancy 79.2%, 78.1%, 78.3%, 76.3%, 69.3%, 78.4%. SitRep66's 798 is a single-cycle +92 outlier that reverts to +3 the next cycle; a value of 708 would make the capacity series monotonic (693, 693, 700, 706, 708, 709) and would have printed 78.1% occupancy, on the same ~78% plateau as every neighbouring cycle. 708 differs from 798 by one digit in the tens place. The most economical reading is a data-entry slip in SitRep66 that propagated to both its bed count and its derived occupancy (and to the national 939 = 798 + 141, which would have been 849). SitRep66's printed values are preserved as published and never silently corrected; what is corrected here is the INTERPRETATION. There was no capacity contraction this cycle: Ituri capacity has grown steadily all week and SitRep67's 78.4% is a RETURN TO TREND, not a deterioration. SitRep66's 69.3% was the anomaly. Recovered advanced +13 to 482 DRC cumulative (all in Ituri), against 27 deaths and 96 non-case exits over the same 24 hours; country-scope recovered 493 with the 11 Uganda anchor.
highlights: 50 new confirmed cases (Ituri 42, Nord-Kivu 8) and 32 new deaths (Ituri 27, Nord-Kivu 5) take the DRC cumulative cleanly to 2473 confirmed / 999 deaths (CFR 40.4%) with no harmonization this cycle. New confirmations fell 79 -> 50 while deaths fell only 37 -> 32, so the day's death-to-case ratio rose to 0.64 from 0.47. Deaths and confirmations of the same day are not the same cohort (deaths lag exposure and confirmation), so this is a reporting-ratio movement and NOT a case-fatality estimate; the cumulative CFR moved 39.9% -> 40.4%. Laboratory positives (42 + 8 = 50) equal the day's confirmations exactly.

NO new affected health zone was reported. The roster holds at 47 touched, 46 actively transmitting, and every cumulative zone delta equals that zone's printed day column, so nothing was silently restated. Ituri's new cases concentrate at Bunia (18), Nizi (9), Rwampara (7), with Nia-Nia and Ariwara at 3 each; Ituri holds 89.0% of cumulative cases and 84.0% of the day's confirmations. Miti-Murhesa (Sud-Kivu) reaches 54 days without a confirmed case.

The reported national contact-follow-up 'improvement' to 82.0% (9623/11739) from 81.1% is a COMPOSITION effect, not a performance gain. Haut-Uele, which reported 52.3% (162/310) at SitRep66, is ND this cycle and leaves the denominator; Tshopo returns at 100.0% (75/75). Holding Haut-Uele's last reported block in place would put the national figure at 81.2%. Within provinces the picture is flat to worse: Ituri 81.3% -> 81.8% and Nord-Kivu 83.8% -> 81.9%. The same caution applies to alert investigation, where the national rate rose to 84.1% while the EPICENTRE fell again, Ituri 75.6% -> 72.8% with 134 alerts uninvestigated; the national gain is carried by Nord-Kivu's large 91.7% block (737/804).

16 of the day's 32 confirmed deaths were community deaths detected by post-mortem swab (Ituri 13 of 27, 48.1%), against 16 in-CTE deaths. A community-death share at half of all confirmed deaths is a surveillance-reach signal: those chains were not under care when the patient died. 322 suspect cases were validated on the day (220 living, 102 community deaths).

alerts_total.data_gap_note: Tableau 3 (at 20/07): 1310 alerts of the day (1239 new + 71 Report-J-1) across Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Tshopo and Sud-Kivu; Haut-Uele is ND on every alert row this cycle and is excluded from the denominators rather than counted as zero. Province rows sum exactly on every column (493+804+4+9 = 1310 reported; 359+737+3+2 = 1101 investigated; 132+83+3+2 = 220 living; 69+33+0+0 = 102 community deaths; 201+116+3+2 = 322 suspects, and 220 + 102 = 322). The national investigation rate 1101/1310 = 84.1% as printed, but it is volume-weighted toward Nord-Kivu (737/804 = 91.7%) and MASKS the epicentre: Ituri fell 75.6% -> 72.8% (359/493), leaving 134 alerts uninvestigated. Tshopo's printed rate of 75.5% does not match its own row (3/4 = 75.0%); the computed 75.0% is promoted and the printed value preserved.

challenges.finding: Reticence toward post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting EDS teams (attack at the Muchanga bridge, activities paralysed at Nyankunde) delay confirmation and under-estimate cases.
challenges.response: Intensify CREC/RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure the teams and increase the number of EDS teams.

challenges.finding: Non-payment of responders (strike in the Bunia and Rwampara health zones; resumption announced after the intervention of Ituri's military governor) interrupts response activities including safe and dignified burials.
challenges.response: Regularise responder payment and secure dedicated financing.

challenges.finding: Insufficient CTE/CT capacity: occupancy 128.4% in Nord-Kivu (141 beds) and 78.4% in Ituri (556 patients for 709 beds), raising admission delays and nosocomial transmission risk.
challenges.response: Accelerate CTE construction and expansion, deploy temporary structures and report bed capacity systematically.

challenges.finding: Contact-tracing performance remains weak: Ituri 81.8%, Nord-Kivu 81.9%, both far below the 95% operational target, leaving transmission chains uninterrupted.
challenges.response: Train, deploy and motivate community relays (RECO) with reinforced supervision.

challenges.finding: Insufficient ambulances and pre-positioning at control points cause transfer and isolation delays.
challenges.response: Pre-position ambulances including at PoE/PoC and deploy transit centres by health zone.

challenges.finding: Insufficient supply of essential medicines (MEG) and medical inputs weakens holistic case management.
challenges.response: Advocacy and urgent procurement of essential medicines.

challenges.finding: Insufficient IPC inputs (PPE, chlorine) and limited functional triage units (175 of 1170, 15%) drive high nosocomial infection risk, with 121 first-line personnel infected and 36 dead.
challenges.response: Urgent procurement and reinforced IPC training.

challenges.finding: Geographic extension (Haut-Uele, Tshopo) and high mobility raise the risk of urban, riverine and cross-border diffusion.
challenges.response: Activate the 23 priority PoE/PoC in Haut-Uele and reinforce cross-border coordination.

challenges.finding: Installation of proximity laboratories (Butembo, Mambasa and Logo) is incomplete, leaving long confirmation delays and undetected transmission.
challenges.response: Accelerate deployment of decentralised diagnostic capacity.

challenges.finding: Insufficient financial resources limit implementation across the response pillars.
challenges.response: Urgent resource mobilisation and advocacy with partners.

challenges.finding: Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) restrict operations.
challenges.response: Reinforce security coordination and humanitarian access.

challenges.finding: Continuity of essential (non-Ebola) health services is compromised, raising indirect mortality.
challenges.response: Effective implementation of free care and reinforcement of essential-service continuity.

priorities.priority: Reverse the alert-investigation fall in the epicentre (Ituri 72.8%, 134 alerts uninvestigated) rather than reading the volume-weighted national 84.1%, and restore Haut-Uele alert and contact reporting, ND on every row this cycle.
Lift Ituri (81.8%) and Nord-Kivu (81.9%) toward the 95% target; the national move to 82.0% is a composition effect from Haut-Uele leaving the denominator, not a performance gain.

Relieve Nord-Kivu isolation saturation at 128.4% (181 of 141 beds), the one genuine capacity emergency on this surface, and restore ND bed reporting in Haut-Uele and Tshopo. Ituri needs no capacity investigation this cycle: its 78.4% is on trend and SitRep66's 69.3% was an outlier produced by a 798-bed figure that does not fit its own series.

Address the community-death share (16 of 32 confirmed deaths, Ituri 13 of 27 at 48.1%) with active case-finding and safe-burial coverage; deaths detected only at post-mortem swab mark chains that were never under care.

Complete decentralised diagnostic capacity (Logo now installed; Butembo and Mambasa outstanding) and explain the Ituri documented-sample contraction 167 -> 113 before positivity movements are read as prevalence.
Sustain residual surveillance in Sud-Kivu, where Miti-Murhesa reaches 54 days without a confirmed case and contact follow-up is closed, toward a provincial end-of-outbreak declaration.

SitRep66's Ituri bed count of 798 (national 939) is an OUTLIER against its own series and is preserved as printed rather than corrected. Ituri bed capacity across SitRep62-67 reads 693, 693, 700, 706, 798, 709, and occupancy 79.2%, 78.1%, 78.3%, 76.3%, 69.3%, 78.4%. SitRep66's 798 is a single-cycle +92 outlier that reverts to +3 the next cycle; a value of 708 would make the capacity series monotonic (693, 693, 700, 706, 708, 709) and would have printed 78.1% occupancy, on the same ~78% plateau as every neighbouring cycle. 708 differs from 798 by one digit in the tens place. The most economical reading is a data-entry slip in SitRep66 that propagated to both its bed count and its derived occupancy (and to the national 939 = 798 + 141, which would have been 849). SitRep66's printed values are preserved as published and never silently corrected; what is corrected here is the INTERPRETATION. There was no capacity contraction this cycle: Ituri capacity has grown steadily all week and SitRep67's 78.4% is a RETURN TO TREND, not a deterioration. SitRep66's 69.3% was the anomaly. Consequence for readers: the apparent occupancy jump from 69.3% to 78.4% must NOT be reported as isolation pressure building in Ituri. Nord-Kivu's 128.4% (181/141) is unchanged across both cycles and remains genuine saturation.

National contact follow-up 82.0% (9623/11739) is NOT a performance improvement over SitRep66's 81.1%, despite the source prose describing a 'legere amelioration'. Haut-Uele reported 52.3% (162/310) last cycle and is ND here, leaving the denominator; Tshopo returns at 100.0% (75/75) and Sud-Kivu closes at 0/0 (NA). Carrying Haut-Uele's last reported block forward gives 81.2%. Within provinces Ituri rose only 81.3% -> 81.8% and Nord-Kivu FELL 83.8% -> 81.9%. The source's own challenge table asks to investigate a 'chute observee en Ituri' that did not occur this cycle.

National alert investigation 84.1% (1101/1310) likewise masks the epicentre. Ituri fell 75.6% -> 72.8% (359/493) with 134 alerts uninvestigated, while the national figure is carried by Nord-Kivu's 737/804 = 91.7% on a much larger alert volume. Haut-Uele is ND on every alert row. Tshopo's printed investigation rate of 75.5% does not match its own row (3/4 = 75.0%); the computed value is promoted.

Tableau 5 is promoted. Sud-Kivu's 4 prose-only PoE/PoC alerts fall outside Tableau 5's two-province scope and are not folded into the global totals.

The day's death-to-case ratio (32 deaths against 50 confirmations = 0.64, up from 0.47) is a reporting-ratio movement, not a case-fatality estimate: same-day deaths and same-day confirmations are different cohorts because deaths lag exposure and confirmation. review_notes: SitRep #067 (report date 2026-07-20; cover publication 2026-07-21; INSP WordPress post 25178, media 25179; WP publish 2026-07-22T08:55:19Z). Full-source reconciliation: national 2473/999 closes from the zone table on every province; the cumulative is cleanly additive from SitRep66 (2423 + 50; 967 + 32); every zone's cumulative delta equals its printed day column; the alert table, contact table, isolation split and bed identity all close exactly; and laboratory positives equal the day's confirmations.

Two source defects preserved rather than propagated: the section-7 PECH pillar prose is a stale reprint of SitRep66's case-management blocks for both Ituri and Nord-Kivu, and the section-3.4.1 PoE/PoC prose disagrees with Tableau 5 on Ituri alert counts. Structured tables promoted in both cases.
